name: AL-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Prediction markets price Rogers near certain
model.rationale: The R+23 district, an entrenched incumbent, and a 35-to-1 fundraising advantage leave Democrat Lee McInnis with no visible path, and markets price Rogers at 99%. Nothing in the evidence suggests movement beyond a few points toward the challenger.
model.watch: A major scandal or unexpected incumbent retirement would be the only realistic opening for Democrats in this seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 3rd District is a deeply Republican seat, and incumbent Mike Rogers is running for re-election with every structural advantage. His challenger, Lee McInnis, has raised about $61,000 and holds under $10,000 on hand, while Rogers has raised $2.1 million and sits on $2.6 million. No independent polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Rogers roughly a 99% chance of winning.

The forecast rests on the district's strong partisan lean, incumbency, and the lopsided money race. A Democratic upset would require an extraordinary outside event, such as a major scandal, since no polling or spending signals suggest the race is competitive.
